desc:
The strings s and t have the same length. Turning s[i] into t[i] costs |s[i] - t[i]|, the absolute difference of their positions in the alphabet (so a to d costs 3).

You may spend at most maxCost in total. Choose a substring of s, i.e. a range of indices [i, j], and convert it to the substring of t at the same indices. Return the maximum length of a range whose conversion cost is at most maxCost.

s = "abcd", t = "bcdf", maxCost = 3
costs per index: 1 1 1 2
indices 0..2 cost 3
result = 3
constraints: s and t contain only lowercase English letters
hints: First turn the two strings into one array of per-index costs.
The question becomes: longest subarray of non-negative numbers with sum at most maxCost.
Use two pointers. Add the cost at right, and while the total exceeds maxCost subtract the cost at left and advance it.
editorial: Compute cost[i] = |s[i] - t[i]|. All costs are non-negative, so the cost of a range grows when it is extended and shrinks when it is trimmed. This is the standard variable-size window: expand to the right, and contract from the left only while the budget is exceeded.
The window never needs to move left, so each index is added once and removed at most once. Time O(n), space O(1) if you compute the costs on the fly instead of storing them.
solution:
def equalSubstring(s, t, maxCost):
    left = 0
    spent = 0
    best = 0
    for right in range(len(s)):
        spent += abs(ord(s[right]) - ord(t[right]))
        while spent > maxCost:
            spent -= abs(ord(s[left]) - ord(t[left]))
            left += 1
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)
    return best
